name: Helsa Cottage Kitchen
why_it_matters: Mon district has almost no commercial restaurants — Helsa Cottage's kitchen is the most-cited dining option in town. Property is run by the head-woman of the family; 'Helsa' is an acronym of her five children's names (Hamwang, Ethiel, Lemnon, Suzanne, Angam). Konyak cottages with a shared kitchen serving traditional slow-cooked pork and bamboo-shoot dishes; Outlook Traveller, Tripadvisor and multiple tour operators flag it as the de facto food stop for Mon-Longwa travellers.
insider_tip: Order meals at check-in or by phone the day before — the kitchen runs a fixed menu, not à la carte. Veg can be arranged but the pork is what they're known for. Tariffs ~₹1000-1500 a night with meals charged separately.

name: Vinngoi Resort Restaurant
why_it_matters: Hilltop resort restaurant with panoramic views over Mon town — modern cottage-resort built around Konyak architectural cues. Kitchen runs local Konyak delicacies plus continental options for travellers who can't do back-to-back smoked pork. Complimentary breakfast included for guests; non-guests can dine on call-ahead.
insider_tip: Useful as a sit-down option if you're not staying at Helsa Cottage — call ahead, mention you're a non-resident, and ask whether the day's smoked pork has been done with axone or bamboo shoot. They also run a budget dormitory above if Helsa is full.

name: Konyak Tea Retreat (Phejin Konyak)
why_it_matters: Tea-estate retreat (est. 1988) outside Shiyong village in Sayeang Tea Estate, run by Phejin Konyak — great-granddaughter of the tattooed headhunter Ahon (one of the first interpreters in J.H. Hutton's 1923 Naga Hills tours) and author of 'The Konyaks: Last of the Tattooed Headhunters' (Roli Books, Silver Award London Book Fair 2018). Phejin cooks for guests herself, sharing stories from her fieldwork during meals.
insider_tip: Booking-only — meals are part of the stay package, not walk-in. Drive ~30km from Mon town; pair with a Longwa visit on the same trip. Phejin's book is on the shelf; ask her to walk you through the tattoo glossary at dinner.

name: Jeilei's Homestay Kitchen
why_it_matters: Inside Longwa — the famous Konyak village whose chief's (Angh's) house spans the India-Myanmar border. Jeilei's homestay has a massive kitchen with a central fireplace where food is slow-cooked Konyak-style. Outlook Traveller and FootLooseDev cite it as the cleanest, friendliest kitchen in Longwa for backpackers and tribal-travel groups.
insider_tip: Roughly ₹600/bed and ₹180-200 per meal (veg/non-veg). Sit at the central fireplace, sip the black tea slowly, and let the food come when it comes — the kitchen runs on family rhythm, not service speed. Longwa has no hotels; this is the food infrastructure.
